core_obligations: Construct the canonical map RGamma_Z(X, K) -> RGamma_Z(X, K_ab) using that Gamma_Z is a functor on abelian sheaves (proof lines 8734-8737).

Show that this map, together with the canonical maps of the abelian-comparison lemma, fits into a morphism of distinguished triangles whose three vertices are RGamma_Z, RGamma and RGamma(U) for K and for K_ab (proof lines 8737-8748).
Conclude that the first arrow is an isomorphism because the other two are, by the five lemma in the derived category (proof lines 8749-8757).
Obtain the sheaf-level statement R-H_Z(K) -> R-H_Z(K_ab) in the same way.
proof_roadmap: Build the comparison map from functoriality of sections with support.
Fit it into a morphism of distinguished triangles.
Apply the five lemma using the known comparisons for global sections.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the canonical maps RGamma_Z(X, K) -> RGamma_Z(X, K_ab) and R-H_Z(K) -> R-H_Z(K_ab), where K_ab is the image of K in the derived category of abelian sheaves, are isomorphisms. The proof builds the first map from the functoriality of Gamma_Z on abelian sheaves and shows that it fits with the canonical maps of the abelian-comparison lemma into a morphism of distinguished triangles coming from the sections-with-support triangle; since two of the three arrows are known isomorphisms, the five lemma in the derived category gives the third (proof lines 8724-8757). The sheaf-level statement is then deduced in the same manner. H2: the triangle comparison and the conclusion by the five lemma are the substance.
